messages:
jamie: Heads-up — customer Foxtrot reported traffic hitting the wrong model variant during a region failover. They have 3 matching rules: org-pin, header-allowlist, and a tenant-level zip-range. Which one should win?
sarah: ugh. order of precedence is messy today. currently we evaluate rules by specificity then created_at fallback. not great for exceptions.
kevin: we should make explicit tie-breaker weights. i.e., rule.weight int; higher wins. keeps behaviour deterministic and lets us surface conflicts in the console.
maria: +1 for weight. but also need a manual escape for support (breakglass) that overrides weights but is auditable. audit trail + TTL.
jamie: idea: precedence: 1) org-pin (force-route), 2) breakglass (short-lived admin pin), 3) explicit rule.weight, 4) header-allowlist, 5) zip-range fallback. does that cover most enterprise asks?
sarah: curious: why put org-pin above breakglass? feels like breakglass should be last-resort override.
kevin: org-pin is customer contract-backed — if they paid for dedicated path we should honor it before any ad-hoc ops breakglass. breakglass is ops-only emergency tool, so it can be lower than contract pins.
maria: ok. we need guardrails: breakglass requires approver + reason + auto-revoke. UI should show who used it and link to audit log.
jamie: agreed. also need to handle header tie cases: multiple headers present, e.g., x-rd-org and x-rd-tenant. Which header do we prefer?
sarah: prefer x-rd-org over tenant header when org-pin exists. otherwise prefer most-specific header (tenant) then org, but again weight can override.
kevin: routing-bot: rule-eval(v1) started for request id abc123 -> matched rules: [zip-range(id:14, weight:10), header-allowlist(id:9, weight:10)] -> tie on weight -> apply header-first policy -> routed to model-a.
jamie: hmm routing-bot sample shows header-first tie-breaker — we should codify. propose tie-breaker flow: 1) explicit force pins (org-pin) 2) breakglass if active 3) highest weight 4) if weight tie -> header matches beat geo/zip rules 5) if still tie -> oldest rule wins (deterministic).
sarah: that seems reasonable. can we also emit a telemetry field on decision path so console can show "why this route was chosen"? e.g., route_decision: ["weight:10","header:tenant:foo"]
maria: yes pls. makes debugging way easier. and add a signal for "contracted_path=true" so billing/SLAs can cross-check.
kevin: quick pseudo impl:
```
matches = find_matches(req)
if matches.any(m => m.type=="org_pin") -> choose org_pin
else if breakglass.active_for(req.org) -> choose breakglass
else best = matches.sort_by(weight, is_header_match, -created_at).first
```
we'll also record decision_trace = matches.map(...)
jamie: perfect. next steps: kevin can add weight field to rule schema + decision_trace to telemetry; sarah will spec console change to surface conflict UI; maria will draft breakglass audit flow and TTL; i'll update runbook.
kevin: i'll make a PR for schema change and unit tests. estimate 2 days.
sarah: i'll add a new panel in route detail page that shows evaluation trace and a conflict warning if multiple high-weight matches.
maria: i'll write playbook for ops breakglass: approval process + auto-revoke + email alerts.
jamie: thanks team. created follow-up ticket: https://redwood.internal/issue/PLAT-8723 (summary: tie-breaker weights + breakglass + telemetry). tagging for visibility. :thumbsup:
